claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances establish a deviation well over tolerance: the trip was recorded at 22.0 km against a recommended-route distance of 19.7 km, a 2.30 km deviation (11.7%) — more than twice POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace confirms which route was actually driven: its road labels run Airport Boulevard, then Pan-Island Expressway (PIE) from 14:36:50, then Sims Way, then Lavender Street and Victoria Street, and never show the recommended East Coast Parkway. The trip record's own events mark the departure from the recommended route at the Airport Boulevard / PIE-ECP split at 14:36:54 and the rejoin at Victoria Street / Lavender Street at 14:58:48. This is a recorded reroute, not a rider's impression, so rows (a), (c) and (e) of the POL-RD-24 matrix (each requiring a deviation within tolerance) are unavailable to the driver.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires him to do before or at the point of deviation. The chat log holds exactly two messages and both concern the pick-up point ('I'm at pick-up point lane B, black Noah' and 'Ok coming out with 2 luggage') — nothing about the route. The trip record's own derived field messages_during_trip is an empty list, the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, and no call recording is in the record at all. Under POL-RD-21 a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established; the notice limb therefore fails on the record.

The driver's answer that 'passenger never say anything during the ride' does not help him. POL-RD-21 places the duty to inform on the driver, and makes the deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. Silence is not acknowledgment, and the chat log here is complete — two entries, truncated false, matching chat_message_count — so there is no missing message in which notice could have been given. The informational failure in POL-RD-21 is made out on the driver's own account as much as on the log.

No traffic justification exists under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory for the recommended road at the trip time — ECP towards City, between Tanah Merah Coast Road and Benjamin Sheares Bridge, a window that overlaps the trip — records advisory type NONE, speed bands 5 to 7 throughout, and states in terms that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded. Its derived finding is justifies_reroute false, and 'NONE' is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (closure, congestion, incident). The driver's bare assertion that 'ECP sometimes jam near Marina' is precisely the driver's assertion without such data that POL-RD-23 says does not justify the reroute.

Row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the rider recovers the excess distance fare in full. The reroute is not traffic-justified, the rider was not informed, and the deviation exceeds 1.0 km; that is row (d) exactly, and the matrix pays the whole excess distance fare. On the ledger's own arithmetic the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 2.30 km x 0.92 SGD = 2.12 SGD, which is the figure the fare breakdown derives at derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd. Because the fare stands at payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, a PARTIAL_REFUND of that sum is what stops the rider carrying the disputed excess distance charge.

This case is one the AI can decide, and an escalation is not required. The contested amount, 36.30 SGD, sits in POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 band, so a ruling stands at a confidence of 0.80, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0), so the 0.95 uplift does not apply. POL-RD-25's separate 2 km limb does not bite here, because the loaded policy holds that limb in route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied and that field is false — it is applied only when true. Nor is POL-GEN-26 engaged: every fact the matrix needs is on the record — both recorded distances, a complete chat log, a complete trace and an available traffic advisory.

I concede this much. The rider asks for the whole 36.30 SGD fare back, but the route-deviation matrix does not provide it: POL-RD-24's remedy is the excess distance fare, which is 2.12 SGD, and POL-GEN-03 defines PARTIAL_REFUND as part of the trip's charge returned. The balance of the metered fare — base, distance, time, airport surcharge and platform fee for the 19.7 km the rider would have travelled anyway — is not recoverable under this policy, and I do not ask the judge to invent it. The rider's win on this record is the 2.12 SGD excess distance fare.

claims.text: The rider asks for the entire 36.30 SGD metered fare back, but no row of the route-deviation matrix returns a trip fare: the only sum POL-RD-24 ever pays is the excess distance fare, which on this record is the deviation of 2.30 km at fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.92 with no surge — 2.12 SGD. The remaining 34.18 SGD of the contested amount is unsupported by the policy, and under POL-GEN-03 the present state stands as to it: the fare ledger records the fare as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and no clause licenses disturbing the fare earned for the distance and time of the recommended route.

The deviation is fixed the way POL-RD-22 directs, and it cannot be inflated beyond that: 22.0 km actual minus 19.7 km recommended, both distances carried on a COMPLETE trip record at weight 1.0, giving 2.30 km. POL-RD-22 provides that the GPS trace shows which route was taken and when and is not used to re-measure the distance, so the recorded distances govern, and the excess distance fare is 2.30 x 0.92 = 2.12 SGD without surge, exactly as the fare breakdown's own derivation records. 2.12 SGD is the largest sum any row of POL-RD-24 can reach on this record.

The record shows one bounded route change, not the whole-ride detour the claim asserts: a single route_deviation_detected event at 14:36:54 at the Airport Boulevard PIE/ECP split and a single route_rejoined event at 14:58:48 at Victoria Street / Lavender Street, over a driver trace of 54 fixes at 30 s intervals from 14:33:20 to 14:59:50 with 100% coverage, every fix map-matched to a road and no interval above 30 s. The extra travel is 2.30 km and about 2.8 minutes on a 19.7 km, 23.7-minute journey; that is the whole of the departure from the recommended route.

The absence of a stated reason for the deviation does not raise the sum the driver must return. POL-RD-24 pays the same excess distance fare on row (b), where the reroute is traffic-justified but the rider is not informed, as on row (d), where it is not traffic-justified at all. Whether the judge treats the driver's in-app chat — which ends at 14:32:20, before the 14:36:54 deviation, and carries no route message — as satisfying POL-RD-21 or not, the figure is 2.12 SGD either way, and the notice question adds nothing to it.

The driver does not contend that traffic data justified the reroute: the only advisory in the file is a type NONE record for the recommended East Coast Parkway segment, speed bands 5-7, recording no incident, roadwork or closure in the trip window, so POL-RD-23 is not met by it — nor by the driver's own assertion of ECP jams in his statement, which POL-RD-23 says cannot justify a reroute without such data. That concession does not cost the fare, because the consequence POL-RD-24 attaches to a reroute that is not traffic-justified is confined to the excess distance fare of 2.12 SGD.

Every artifact the matrix requires is on file and unimpaired: the GPS trace, trip record, fare breakdown, chat log and traffic advisory each carry admissibility status COMPLETE with no issue codes and weight_multiplier 1.0, so no fact POL-RD-24 needs is unestablished and POL-GEN-26 is not engaged. The case therefore falls to be decided on the matrix rather than inferred from any absence, and the 2 km ceiling on an AI ruling in v2.1 6.2 is expressly held unapplied in this policy version — ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false — so the 2.30 km deviation does not of itself displace an AI ruling under POL-RD-25.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the 36.30 SGD fare dispute is decided under the route-deviation matrix (POL-RD-24), the deviation measure (POL-RD-22) and the traffic-justification rule (POL-RD-23).

What the record establishes. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-05010, status COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records 22.0 km driven against a recommended-route distance of 19.7 km — a 2.30 km deviation, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances establish a deviation well over tolerance: the trip was recorded at 22.0 km against a recommended-route distance of 19.7 km, a 2.30 km deviation (11.7%) — more than twice POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace confirms which route was actually driven: its road labels run Airport Boulevard, then Pan-Island Expressway (PIE) from 14:36:50, then Sims Way, then Lavender Street and Victoria Street, and never show the recommended East Coast Parkway. The trip record's own events mark the departure from the recommended route at the Airport Boulevard / PIE-ECP split at 14:36:54 and the rejoin at Victoria Street / Lavender Street at 14:58:48. This is a recorded reroute, not a rider's impression, so rows (a), (c) and (e) of the POL-RD-24 matrix (each requiring a deviation within tolerance) are unavailable to the driver.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires him to do before or at the point of deviation. The chat log holds exactly two messages and both concern the pick-up point ('I'm at pick-up point lane B, black Noah' and 'Ok coming out with 2 luggage') — nothing about the route. The trip record's own derived field messages_during_trip is an empty list, the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, and no call recording is in the record at all. Under POL-RD-21 a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established; the notice limb therefore fails on the record.

The driver's answer that 'passenger never say anything during the ride' does not help him. POL-RD-21 places the duty to inform on the driver, and makes the deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. Silence is not acknowledgment, and the chat log here is complete — two entries, truncated false, matching chat_message_count — so there is no missing message in which notice could have been given. The informational failure in POL-RD-21 is made out on the driver's own account as much as on the log.

No traffic justification exists under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory for the recommended road at the trip time — ECP towards City, between Tanah Merah Coast Road and Benjamin Sheares Bridge, a window that overlaps the trip — records advisory type NONE, speed bands 5 to 7 throughout, and states in terms that no incident, roadwork or closure was recorded. Its derived finding is justifies_reroute false, and 'NONE' is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (closure, congestion, incident). The driver's bare assertion that 'ECP sometimes jam near Marina' is precisely the driver's assertion without such data that POL-RD-23 says does not justify the reroute.

Row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies and the rider recovers the excess distance fare in full. The reroute is not traffic-justified, the rider was not informed, and the deviation exceeds 1.0 km; that is row (d) exactly, and the matrix pays the whole excess distance fare. On the ledger's own arithmetic the excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 2.30 km x 0.92 SGD = 2.12 SGD, which is the figure the fare breakdown derives at derived.money.excess_distance_fare_sgd. Because the fare stands at payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.0, a PARTIAL_REFUND of that sum is what stops the rider carrying the disputed excess distance charge.

This case is one the AI can decide, and an escalation is not required. The contested amount, 36.30 SGD, sits in POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 band, so a ruling stands at a confidence of 0.80, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0), so the 0.95 uplift does not apply.
